g_81e2fc5c1b7d:
Sealed envelope — Nook's unit of storage.
*
Everything written to disk goes through here. Nothing else in the project
calls `crypto.subtle` to encrypt user data.
*
The choice worth explaining is `context`. On top of the content, AES-GCM
authenticates an associated datum that is not encrypted. We put the
record's location in it. The consequence: an attacker with disk access
cannot *relocate* an envelope — copying the contents of `docs/A` into
`docs/B` produces an authentication failure instead of a silent
substitution. Without it, encryption would protect confidentiality but not
the integrity of the structure.

g_8971a9d39040:
The "zero network" guard.
*
The rule is really enforced by the CSP (`connect-src 'none'`): not even a
malicious dependency can get out. This script is the canary — it fails CI
*at the moment* code capable of emitting a request enters the bundle,
rather than at the moment a user notices.
*
It inspects the build, not the sources: what matters is what is actually
served, dependencies included.
*
Two distinct corpora, because they do not have the same rights:
  - application code may not call any network API;
  - the service worker, on the other hand, MUST call `fetch` — that is its
    whole purpose — but may not mention any external origin.
*
Every exception goes through ALLOWED and must carry a readable reason. The
exceptions in force are reprinted on each run: a waiver nobody sees again
is a waiver nobody ever re-examines.

g_8cacd81517a8:
Access to IndexedDB.
*
Deliberately narrow: open, read, write, erase. No notion of a document, of
encryption or of the interface gets in here — this module only knows how to
handle opaque key/value pairs.
*
One IndexedDB constraint governs the shape of this API: a transaction
auto-closes as soon as the microtask queue drains with no request pending.
Awaiting a non-IndexedDB promise in the middle of a transaction therefore
kills it silently. That is why there is no generic `transact(db, fn)` here:
encryption, being asynchronous, must be finished *before* the transaction
opens. `writeBatch` is the only atomic primitive on offer, and it takes
only values that are already prepared.

g_b53295fbbe1c:
A stand-in for `emoji-mart`, substituted at build time.
*
The emoji-picker library fetches its localisation data *and* its images
from a CDN, at runtime. That is incompatible with Nook's promise: the CSP
would block those requests, and the picker would be silently broken — the
worst of the two situations, since the user would see a feature that does
not work without knowing why.
*
Disabling it with an option was not enough: the code still went into the
served files, and would have stayed there at the mercy of a future setting.
An alias in `vite.config.ts` therefore replaces it with this module, and
the network guard observes its absence.
*
What is lost: the emoji menu triggered by typing ":". Emoji typed on the
system keyboard work normally.
*
This module stands in for `emoji-mart` and for `@emoji-mart/data` alike: the
first reads functions, the second a data object, and the empty default
export suits both.
